stem: A positive ion of charge +2.0 μC experiences an electric force of 0.010 N to the right. What is the electric field at its position?
explanation: E = F/q = 0.010/(2.0 × 10⁻⁶) = 5.0 × 10³ N C⁻¹, in the same direction as the force on the positive ion.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: An electron is released from rest between two horizontal plates. The upper plate is at a higher electric potential than the lower plate. Which way does the electron initially accelerate?
explanation: The electric field is downward, from higher to lower potential. The force on a negative charge is opposite the electric field, so the electron accelerates upward.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: A proton is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 500 V. What kinetic energy does it gain?
explanation: The energy gained by one elementary positive charge through 500 V is 500 eV (8.0 × 10⁻¹⁷ J).
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: A positive ion enters the uniform electric field between vertical plates with an initial velocity horizontally to the right, as shown. Neglect gravity. How does the ion move?
options: In a straight horizontal line, slowing down
In a straight horizontal line, speeding up
explanation: The electric field is from the positive left plate towards the negative right plate. The positive ion accelerates to the right, parallel to its initial velocity. Its path remains horizontal and its speed increases.
diagramAlt: Positive ion moving to the right between vertical charged plates with the field directed right.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: A particle of charge +3.0 × 10⁻⁶ C and mass 2.0 × 10⁻³ kg is in a uniform horizontal electric field of 400 N C⁻¹. What is its acceleration, neglecting gravity?

stem: A charged particle moves at speed v through a uniform magnetic field of flux density B, making an angle of 30° with the field. The charge magnitude is q. What is the magnetic force magnitude?
explanation: F = qvB sin θ = qvB sin 30° = qvB/2.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: An electron travels horizontally to the right into a magnetic field directed into the page, as shown. What is the initial direction of the magnetic force on the electron?
explanation: For a positive charge moving right with B into the page, v × B is up. An electron is negatively charged, so the force is down.
diagramAlt: An electron travels to the right into a magnetic field shown by crosses.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: A charged particle follows a circular path in a uniform magnetic field with its velocity perpendicular to the field. Which quantity remains unchanged?
explanation: Magnetic force is perpendicular to the velocity and performs no work, so speed and kinetic energy remain constant; velocity and momentum directions change.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: A particle moves in a circular orbit of radius r in a uniform magnetic field. Its speed is doubled while its mass, charge and field remain unchanged. What is the new radius?
explanation: r = mv/(|q|B). For fixed m, |q| and B, radius is proportional to speed.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: Two ions have the same mass, charge magnitude and speed, but ion X travels in a magnetic field twice as strong as that for ion Y. What is the ratio of their circular-path radii, rₓ/rᵧ?
explanation: With r = mv/(|q|B), doubling B halves the radius: rₓ/rᵧ = 1/2.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: A positive ion travels to the right through perpendicular uniform electric and magnetic fields, as shown. The electric field points upwards and the magnetic field is out of the page. What speed allows the ion to pass through undeflected?
explanation: The electric force qE acts up; for v right and B out of the page, magnetic force qvB is down. Balanced forces require qE = qvB, so v = E/B.
diagramAlt: Positive ion with velocity to the right, upward electric field and magnetic field out of the page.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: In a velocity selector, a beam of singly charged positive ions passes undeflected when v = E/B. If the charge of each ion is doubled with the fields unchanged, what happens to the selected speed?
options: It increases by a factor of four
explanation: Both electric and magnetic forces scale with charge, so q cancels in qE = qvB.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: A velocity selector uses an electric field strength of 3.0 × 10⁴ N C⁻¹ and magnetic flux density 0.20 T. What speed will pass undeflected?

section: Direction of force on a conductor
stem: A straight horizontal wire carries conventional current to the right in a magnetic field directed into the page. What is the magnetic force direction on the wire?
options: Along the wire to the right
explanation: I L × B: right crossed with into the page gives upward force.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: A straight wire carries current in a uniform magnetic field. The angle between the wire and the field changes from 90° to 30°, while all other quantities remain fixed. How does the force change?
explanation: F = BIL sin θ. sin 30°/sin 90° = 1/2.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: Two long parallel wires X and Y carry steady currents in the same direction out of the page, as shown. How do the wires exert magnetic forces on one another?
options: Both wires are attracted towards each other
Both wires are repelled away from each other
X is attracted but Y is repelled
No force acts on either wire
explanation: Parallel currents in the same direction attract. The forces are equal and opposite.
diagramAlt: Two parallel wires labelled X and Y with current out of the page.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: Two long parallel wires carry currents in opposite directions. What is the nature of the magnetic force between them?
options: Attractive for one wire, repulsive for the other
explanation: Parallel wires with opposite current directions repel each other.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: The magnetic force per unit length between two parallel wires is F/L. Both currents are doubled and their separation is halved. What is the new force per unit length?
explanation: F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πr); the product of currents rises fourfold and halving r doubles the force, giving eight times.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: Two long parallel wires carry currents of 3.0 A and 5.0 A, separated by 0.10 m. What is the magnetic force per unit length between them? (μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ N A⁻²)
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: Two identical long straight wires carry equal currents out of the page. Point P lies midway between them, as shown. What is the resultant magnetic flux density at P due to the two wires?
explanation: The magnetic field at P from the left wire points up and from the right wire points down. Equal magnitudes cancel.
diagramAlt: Two identical wires with currents out of page and midpoint P.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: An electron enters an approximately uniform magnetic field inside a long solenoid along the solenoid axis. What is its subsequent motion if no electric field or other forces act?
options: It moves undeflected at constant speed
It follows a circle around the axis
explanation: The velocity is parallel to B; F = |q|vB sin 0° = 0, so the particle continues straight at constant speed.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

section: Comparison of electric and magnetic forces
stem: A positive charge moves through a magnetic field at right angles to its velocity. Separately, the same charge moves along a uniform electric field. Which statement is correct?
options: Both fields necessarily change the particle’s speed
Only the magnetic field can change kinetic energy
Neither field can change the particle’s kinetic energy
The magnetic field changes direction without changing speed; the electric field can change speed
explanation: Magnetic force is perpendicular to velocity and does no work; electric force can have a component along velocity and change kinetic energy.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.

stem: A particle with charge magnitude q and mass m moves in a circle perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of flux density B. What is the period of one complete revolution?
explanation: qvB = mv²/r gives r = mv/(qB). Period T = 2πr/v = 2πm/(qB), independent of speed.
sourceNote: Original question aligned to IB Physics 2025 syllabus; provided D.3 Paper 1A examples used only as difficulty benchmarks.
